notes: Homestead-exemption case; the selector fired on a passing citation to Whyte v. Grant (a different case) where a widow happened to keep a boarding house. This case's own facts involve no letting of rooms or dwellings; it is about who qualifies as 'head of a family' under the homestead article.

Divorce/separation-from-bed-and-board case. A witness mentions the husband boarded temporarily at a Mrs. Taylor's house, but this is incidental testimony about the husband's whereabouts, not an issue of the legal character of letting or lodging.

Municipal ordinance case about impounding cattle running at large as a nuisance; has nothing to do with lodging, boarding, or letting of dwellings. Selector match on generic police-power/nuisance language.

Co-ownership partition/accounting dispute over rents collected from tenants of a property between co-owners; concerns tenancy-in-common accounting, not the legal character of short-term letting or lodging-house regulation. Selector matched on generic possession/occupancy language.

Dispute between hotel-building owner and commercial lessee over trade name and whether renaming 'Hotel Denechaud' to 'The Inn' (and closing the dining room) breached the lease; discusses the inn/hotel distinction only to decide if the lease's use-clause was violated, not the legality or regulation of letting rooms to lodgers. Not scored relevant, but flagging 'European plan'/'American plan' as candidate lexicon terms for the Planner.

Companion case to the same Sieward/Denechaud hotel lease; the only issue here is whether the lessee could be forced to accept a rent-payment reservation clause. No bearing on the legal character of letting or lodging.

Jactitation/slander-of-title suit over a railroad's right of way and servitude across a plantation; concerns prescription, registry, and possession of land, wholly unrelated to letting dwellings or rooms for pay.
Municipal ordinance prohibiting Sunday baseball as 'desecration of the Sabbath'; a police-power/ordinance-validity case, but about Sabbath observance, not lodging or boarding-house regulation.
Dispute over state ownership/leasing of a navigable-stream bed for oil drilling and a servitude of passage; no connection to letting dwellings or rooms.

Tort action for a third party's officious interference with a plantation owner's tenant and sharecroppers, causing loss of the owner's rental share; involves agricultural leasing/rent-in-kind, not short-term letting of rooms or dwellings for lodging.

House built and leased for use as a bawdyhouse in the restricted district; the lease is voided as having an immoral object under Civ. Code art. 1892. This concerns illegality of a lease for prostitution, not the legal character of ordinary short-term letting of rooms/dwellings to lodgers or its regulation; excluding despite selector match on 'lease'/'sublease' language.

Conviction for applying a 'residence' building to 'business' use without upgrading construction to Building Code fire-safety standards. This is a general zoning/construction-code enforcement case about occupancy classification, not specifically about lodging or boarding houses; the affidavit never mentions lodgers, boarders, or letting rooms.

Municipal ordinance restricting the location of livery stables, struck down as discriminatory 'location' regulation exceeding the town's charter power. Concerns livery stables, not lodging or boarding houses; no bearing on the target doctrine despite similar police-power reasoning.

Contract conveying land in exchange for lifetime support (nourriture) with a reserved right of use and habitation for the sellers; a sale/support-annuity contract, not a letting of rooms or dwellings for pay to lodgers or transient occupants.
Municipal ordinance prohibiting gambling slot machines; a police-power ordinance-validity case about gambling/lotteries, with no connection to lodging, boarding, or letting of dwellings.
